title: In MENA, the day after the crisis begins today
summary:
As we in the GCC navigate yet another political and security crisis, founders, CEOs and investors need a blunt reminder: cash is the only real buffer.


Liquidity trumps everything. It gives you the confidence to keep building without panic, without knee-jerk decisions, and without sacrificing the people and capabilities you have spent years assembling.


When you have liquidity, you stay focused on products, on clients, on execution – not on firefighting. And when you are scaling, liquidity is what allows you to keep serving customers with discipline and attention even when the world outside is shaking.

title: Venture capital’s most underrated skill: knowing when NOT to invest
summary:
An article by Husameddin AlMadani, angel investor and aviator


There is a moment before every flight that matters more than takeoff itself.


It is not dramatic or cinematic. From the outside, it often looks like nothing at all. A pilot reviews the conditions, studies the route, checks the aircraft, evaluates the weather, considers alternatives, and then makes a decision: go or no-go.


That decision is deceptively simple to underestimate because nothing visibly happens. If the answer is “go”, the flight proceeds. If the answer is “no-go”, the aircraft stays on the ground, the plan changes, and life moves on.


Over time, I have come to believe that this moment — the disciplined willingness to decide whether conditions truly justify action — is one of the most important lessons that flying can offer. For me, it has also become one of the most useful mental models in investing.

title: MENA startups raise $454.7 million in May 2026, led by debt financing
summary:
At first glance, investment activity across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) appears to have rebounded strongly in May 2026. Startups in the region raised a combined $454.7 million across 33 deals, marking a 202% month-on-month increase and a 76% rise compared to May 2025.


However, a closer look shows that most of this growth was driven by debt financing, which made up 66% of the total funding raised during the month. Even without counting debt deals, startups still raised more capital and completed more transactions than in April, indicating a slight increase in investor activity.


Yet the year-on-year picture tells a different story. While capital deployment increased, the deal count declined by 57% compared to May 2025, suggesting that investors remain selective, favouring larger transactions over broader market participation amid continued regional uncertainty.

summary: Doha-based hyperlocal delivery platform Snoonu has acquired an Egyptian Q-commerce startup, marking its first move outside the GCC as it plots a pan-Arab expansion strategy.

title: Saudi Arabia Launches SR10 Billion Venture Debt Facility for Growth-Stage Startups
summary: The Saudi Venture Capital Company (SVC) has announced a SR10 billion venture debt program to address the financing gap for startups between Series B and pre-IPO stages.

title: PIF, TMG Sign MoU To Advance Saudi's Urban Development Ecosystem
summary: Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) and the Saudi subsidiary of Talaat Moustafa Group (TMG) have signed an agreement to explore collaboration on urban development projects, as the kingdom continues to advance its Vision 2030 agenda to improve livability and infrastructure.Agreement details The agreement aims to explore opportunities and collaborate in mixed-use real estate projects at developments owned by the sovereign wealth fund and its projects across the kingdom. It is part of the PIF's broader strategic goals to diversify Saudi Arabia's economy. Under the non-binding agreement, the two parties intend to unlock opportunities across the residential, commercial, hospitality, and retail sectors, as well as integrated urban environments. The partnership combines PIF’s investment capabilities with TMG’s track record in delivering integrated mixed-use developments. title: Egypt’s Foreign Reserves Surge To $53.1B In May, GDP Grows 5.2% In July-March Period
summary: Egypt’s net foreign reserves rose to $53.1 billion at the end of May, while economic growth accelerated to 5.2% in the first nine months of the fiscal year, providing fresh signs that the country’s stabilization efforts are gaining traction.Egypt's economic growth According to data released Sunday by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), net international reserves rose from $53.01 billion in April, signaling sustained liquidity and resilience against external shocks. Simultaneously, a Reuters report citing the Planning Ministry revealed that the country's gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 5.2% in the July–March period of FY 2025/2026, signaling a steady rebound following an aggressive pipeline of structural and economic reforms. title: Bahrain-based Beehive Expands P2P Lending to Saudi SMEs
